note: MOD_PLAN A49 (decode at 10K vs 64K vs 128K: how much of the decode window is attention over the cache). One arm, measurement only: every longdec* case is a cold source-text prompt of 10000 / 32000 / 64000 / 120000 tokens followed by a 256-token reply, metric = decode tok/s of that reply (the engine's own log line); short is the empty-context reference. Read the table as ms per token = 1000 / tok/s; the slope of ms per token over the context length is the attention cost (the rest, the intercept, is expert reads + dense layers). Decision rule for A50 / A51 (attention-saving items): if (ms@128K - ms@10K) is below ~10% of ms@10K the attention share is too small to be worth a sparse-attention item; above ~25% it is. 128K needs --max-context 131072 (the preset has it); each longdec case reads its prompt cold (tens of seconds to a few minutes at 120K), so run it with --tier confirm --reps 3 --no-early-stop only when the GPU is free for ~1 h. Add arms (for example STRATA_ATTN_DAILY=0, or --kv fp16) to see how the slope changes; with two or more arms the usual A/B verdict is printed per case.
